posts.content_md:
I made my very first DCG dim hologram with TEA instead of TMG using 5mW 650nm lasermodule. Exposition time was around 45min. It was great feeling 

I used this composition:

Gelatine………….….…..12g

Water…………………....80ml

TEA acetate………………10ml

K2Cr2O7 5%¤…..…….1ml

MB 0,4%¤.……..6ml

Finaly adjuted pH na 9,0 – 9,5

with 25% solution TEA

Processing was: immersing in potassium thiosulphate, distilled water 25°C, 50% isopropropanol, 100% hot isopropanol

I have picture, but I don't know how to upload it.... 

You can look here, it's hologram of old DX4 processor.

[http://www.digineff.cz/galerie/showphot ... all&page=1](http://www.digineff.cz/galerie/showphoto.php?photo=111364&password=&sort=1&cat=all&page=1)

Congratulations, that's pretty amazing (though not quite a high-speed recording system )!

I thought TEA and dichromates produced some dark reaction... 

Given the quantities of TEA involved, I wonder how tacky a layer had been formed. And what's been the size of the hologram?

posts.author: info.crew
posts.content_md:
> Congratulations, that's pretty amazing (though not quite a high-speed recording system Smile)!I thought TEA and dichromates produced some dark reaction...Given the quantities of TEA involved, I wonder how tacky a layer had been formed. And what's been the size of the hologram?

Yes, the speed was very slow. Unexposed plates were milky, exposed areas were clear. The plate was 5x5cm and fit the processor. I used the high speed spincoating made of the big like PC fan. I didn't make any power meterig. Iteresting is, that there was no shift during exposition, because I live in 8th floor in noisy concrete pannel house. The plates were little bit tacky and my hologram after three reprocessings shift to UV region. I didnt control the temperature also. Now I am experimenting with other organic amines to replace expensive TMG. I will also try my 5mW 532 nm module with "yelowish" eosine (C20H6Br4K2O5) this evening.
